mechanism: Ruvonoflast (NT-0796) is an oral, brain-penetrant small-molecule NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor intended to regulate chronic inflammation across peripheral and central cardiometabolic pathways, including hypothalamic inflammation implicated in weight regulation.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists RESOLVE-1 (NCT07055516) as an active, not recruiting Phase 2 randomized, triple-masked, placebo-controlled trial of oral NT-0796 once daily or twice daily versus placebo as an adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in participants with obesity with or without type 2 diabetes. Actual enrollment is 176; the registry shows an estimated primary and study completion date of May 21, 2026, while NodThera has guided to RESOLVE-1/RESOLVE-2 completion in 3Q 2026.
clinical_summary: RESOLVE-1 is designed to test 24-week change in body weight and hsCRP, with HbA1c assessed in the type 2 diabetes stratum and secondary measures including body composition, waist measures, metabolic biomarkers, pharmacokinetics, safety, tolerability, and suicidality. Prior NodThera Phase 1b/2a cardiovascular-risk data in inflamed obese subjects showed rapid, significant hsCRP reduction versus placebo, with more than 75% of NT-0796-treated subjects reaching hsCRP <=2 mg/L at Day 28 versus less than 25% on placebo; body-weight reductions were most pronounced in high-risk subgroups. Preclinical obesity models showed weight loss comparable to semaglutide or calorie restriction and additive/sustained effects with semaglutide, but human obesity efficacy data from RESOLVE-1 are not yet posted.
safety_summary: No RESOLVE-1 results are posted. ClinicalTrials.gov includes safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic, and suicidality assessments over the 24-week treatment and follow-up period. NodThera reported that prior Phase 1b/2a cardiovascular-risk testing found NT-0796 generally safe and well tolerated, with adverse events mainly mild and transient and no serious adverse events; the company also states clinical studies to date have shown robust tolerability and no gastrointestinal side effects, but detailed peer-reviewed human safety results for the obesity program are not yet available.
management_tools: Pharmacy-benefit prior authorization for obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes
Eligibility criteria requiring adult age, BMI threshold, and obesity-related comorbidity documentation where applicable
Documentation of concurrent reduced-calorie diet, increased physical activity, or structured lifestyle program
Step therapy or preferred-product sequencing against covered anti-obesity medications if label and evidence support positioning
Continuation criteria requiring documented weight-loss response after an initial authorization period
Quantity limit aligned to the final labeled once-daily or twice-daily oral dose
Concurrent-use rules for other anti-obesity agents or GLP-1/GIP therapies based on final label, trial evidence, and payer policy
evidence_gaps: No RESOLVE-1 efficacy or safety results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
The CT.gov estimated primary completion date of May 21, 2026 has passed relative to the packet check date, but the record remains active, not recruiting with April 2026 verification.
No Phase 3 trial, regulatory filing plan, or registrational endpoint strategy has been disclosed for obesity or type 2 diabetes.
NT-0796 has no disclosed commercial price; annual cost is analog-derived from current branded anti-obesity pricing.
Durability of weight loss, HbA1c effect in type 2 diabetes, impact on lean mass, cardiovascular outcomes, and safety with chronic NLRP3 inhibition remain uncertain.
Final payer positioning will depend on whether NT-0796 is labeled as monotherapy, GLP-1 adjunct, follow-on maintenance therapy, or a cardiometabolic-risk therapy.

sources.title: Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of NT-0796 in Participants With Obesity With or Without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
supports: Study acronym is RESOLVE-1; sponsor is NodThera Limited; org study ID is NT-0796-P004.

Official title describes a Phase 2a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of NT-0796 as adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in obese participants with or without type 2 diabetes.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; phase is Phase 2; actual enrollment is 176; actual start date was May 8, 2025; estimated primary and study completion dates are May 21, 2026.
Arms include oral NT-0796 twice daily, oral NT-0796 once daily with placebo second daily dose, and placebo twice daily for up to 24 weeks.

Primary outcomes include hsCRP ratio change in participants without T2DM and body-weight change from baseline to Week 24; secondary outcomes include HbA1c in participants with T2DM, waist/body-composition measures, biomarkers, pharmacokinetics, safety, tolerability, and suicidality.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Effects of NT-0796 in Obese Participants at Risk of Cardiovascular Disease
supports: Completed prior randomized trial of NT-0796 in obese participants at risk of cardiovascular disease.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists Phase 1, actual enrollment of 67, start October 10, 2023, and primary/study completion April 15, 2024.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.

sources.title: Study to Explore the Safety and Efficacy of NT-0796 as an Adjunct to Semaglutide in Participants With Obesity (RESOLVE-2)
supports: Related Phase 2 RESOLVE-2 trial evaluates NT-0796 as an adjunct to semaglutide in participants with obesity.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; estimated enrollment is 82; estimated primary and study completion dates are August 21, 2026.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.

sources.title: NodThera Pipeline
supports: NodThera pipeline names ruvonoflast as NT-0796 and lists RESOLVE-1 (NCT07055516) and RESOLVE-2 (NCT07220629) under cardiometabolic diseases in Phase 2.
Company states ruvonoflast has demonstrated improvements in markers of inflammation, thrombosis, and metabolism and has a large clinical efficacy and safety dataset among current NLRP3 inhibitors.
Company states ruvonoflast has high tissue and brain penetrance with intracellular activation in immune and cardiometabolic cells.

sources.title: NodThera Charts Obesity Future with First Patients Dosed in Phase 2 RESOLVE-1 Trial of Oral NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitor NT-0796
supports: RESOLVE-1 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial of NT-0796 in patients with obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes, over 24 weeks.
Company expected 160 patients randomized to twice-daily oral NT-0796, once-daily oral NT-0796, or placebo.
Primary endpoint is change in body weight from baseline to Week 24; secondary endpoints include body composition, metabolic biomarkers, and HbA1c in participants with type 2 diabetes.
Headline data were anticipated in Q2 2026.
NodThera describes NT-0796 as an oral, brain-penetrant NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor targeting chronic inflammation and weight regulation.

sources.title: NodThera's NLRP3 Inhibitor NT-0796 Meets Primary Endpoint of Inflammation Reversal in Phase Ib/IIa Trial in Obese Subjects with Cardiovascular Risk
supports: Prior Phase 1b/2a cardiovascular-risk study enrolled obese subjects with elevated baseline CRP and at least one cardiovascular risk factor.
Study met the primary endpoint with highly significant and rapid CRP reduction compared with placebo at Day 28.
More than 75% of NT-0796-treated subjects achieved CRP <=2 mg/L at Day 28 compared with less than 25% among placebo.
Company reported reductions in additional pro-inflammatory and cardiometabolic biomarkers and most pronounced placebo-adjusted body-weight reductions in high-risk subgroups.
NT-0796 was generally safe and well tolerated; adverse events were mainly mild and transient and no serious adverse events were observed.

sources.title: NodThera Announces First Patients Dosed in RESOLVE-2 Clinical Trial Evaluating Oral NT-0796 in Combination with a GLP-1 Receptor Agonist
supports: NT-0796 is described as an oral, brain-penetrant NLRP3 inhibitor that selectively regulates chronic inflammation, a driver of cardiometabolic diseases.
NodThera expected to complete RESOLVE-1 and RESOLVE-2 by 3Q 2026.
Company states NT-0796 is being investigated in two Phase 2 obesity trials: monotherapy RESOLVE-1 and GLP-1RA combination RESOLVE-2.
Company states clinical studies to date showed robust safety and tolerability and no gastrointestinal side effects.

sources.title: Reversal of High Fat Diet-Induced Obesity, Systemic Inflammation, and Astrogliosis by the NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitors NT-0249 and NT-0796
supports: Preclinical diet-induced obesity model reported NT-0249/NT-0796 reversed obesity and inflammation in mice.
NLRP3 inhibition matched weight loss driven by semaglutide or calorie restriction in the model.

NLRP3 inhibition showed enhanced improvements in disease-relevant biomarkers of acute phase response, cardiovascular inflammation, and lipid metabolism compared with semaglutide or calorie restriction.

sources.title: The NLRP3 inhibitor NT-0796 enhances and sustains GLP-1R agonist-mediated weight loss in a murine diet-induced obesity model
supports: Preclinical murine diet-induced obesity study evaluated whether NT-0796 could enhance or sustain semaglutide-mediated weight loss.
NodThera reported the NT-0796 plus semaglutide combination produced nearly two-fold greater weight loss than semaglutide alone over 28 days in a high-fat diet model.
Company summary states animals on combination therapy achieved more than 30% weight loss and that NT-0796 monotherapy reduced weight regain after semaglutide cessation.

Used as a high-cost branded obesity analog because NT-0796 has no disclosed price.

Used as a lower branded-obesity analog for annual cost sensitivity.

sources.title: Information for Connecticut Prescribers of Prescription Drugs: Zepbound
supports: Lilly disclosure lists Zepbound pen wholesale acquisition cost as $1,086.37 for a pack of four pens across 2.5 mg to 15 mg strengths.
Lilly disclosure lists direct-to-patient vial prices ranging from $299 to $1,049 depending on dose.
Used as a branded anti-obesity comparator and pricing cross-check.

sources.title: Weight Loss - Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Agonists Prior Authorization Policy
supports: Cigna policy for weight-loss GLP-1/GIP agents includes prior authorization, initial approval periods, baseline BMI criteria, behavioral modification and dietary restriction requirements, and continuation criteria.

Adult weight-loss criteria include BMI >=30 kg/m2 or BMI >=27 kg/m2 with weight-related comorbidity such as type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, sleep apnea, cardiovascular disease, MASLD/NAFLD, or other listed conditions.
Continuation criteria for Wegovy tablet and Zepbound include documented >=5% loss of baseline body weight and continued behavioral modification/reduced-calorie diet.
Cigna considers concomitant use with other GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonists not medically necessary for the analog class.

expected_launch_window.method: Derived from current Phase 2 status, expected 2026 Phase 2 completion/readout, lack of disclosed Phase 3 program, and typical need for Phase 3 obesity/T2D efficacy and safety data plus regulatory review.
expected_launch_window.explanation: Even if RESOLVE-1 is positive in 2026, NT-0796 would likely require at least one multi-year Phase 3 program before launch in obesity or obesity with type 2 diabetes.

annual_cost_range.method: Used branded anti-obesity analogs because NT-0796 has no disclosed price. Low estimate applies NovoCare Wegovy self-pay maintenance pricing of $349/month x 12 = $4,188. High estimate applies NovoCare Wegovy list price of $1,349.02/package x 12 = $16,188.24, rounded to $16,188; Zepbound WAC of $1,086.37 per four-pen pack is a cross-check below the high end.
annual_cost_range.explanation: The range is a gross analog estimate and excludes rebates, discounts, adherence, lab monitoring, visits, cardiometabolic event offsets, or combination use with GLP-1 therapy.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced novel oral brain-penetrant NLRP3 mechanism, prior human anti-inflammatory biomarker signal, and supportive preclinical weight data against absence of posted human obesity efficacy data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: NT-0796 could differentiate on oral dosing, inflammatory-risk biology, tolerability, and potential maintenance or GLP-1 adjunct use, but current evidence has not yet shown Phase 2 human weight-loss or HbA1c efficacy.

budget_impact.method: Assessed from chronic therapy, broad obesity/T2D eligible population, likely pharmacy-benefit utilization, and analog branded anti-obesity annual costs up to about $16k gross.
budget_impact.explanation: Even a moderately priced oral agent could create high aggregate spend if broadly used for obesity, obesity with type 2 diabetes, or GLP-1 maintenance/adjunct strategies.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from Phase 2 status, imminent 2026 data, novel non-incretin oral mechanism, and possible use as monotherapy or GLP-1 adjunct, offset by no registrational data yet.
disruption_risk.explanation: Near-term formulary disruption is limited before Phase 3, but positive RESOLVE-1/2 results could shift payer attention toward oral non-GLP-1 and combination obesity management.

recommended_action.method: Recommended monitoring because the asset is Phase 2 with no posted RESOLVE-1 results, no disclosed Phase 3 plan, no price, and a potentially high-impact but unproven clinical profile.
recommended_action.explanation: Track RESOLVE-1 and RESOLVE-2 readouts, subsequent Phase 3 initiation, and whether efficacy supports monotherapy, GLP-1 adjunct, or weight-maintenance positioning before active formulary planning.

quality_flags: ClinicalTrials.gov estimated primary and study completion date for NCT07055516 is 2026-05-21, which is before the 2026-05-28 packet check date, but the registry status remains active, not recruiting with no posted results.
NodThera's 2025 RESOLVE-1 release expected 160 randomized participants; the current ClinicalTrials.gov API lists actual enrollment of 176.
NT-0796 is now named ruvonoflast on the company pipeline page; some trial and press sources still use NT-0796 only.
Human obesity efficacy, HbA1c effect, and long-term safety are not yet established; key weight-loss differentiation is currently supported mainly by preclinical and biomarker data.
Annual cost range is analog-derived and should be replaced if NodThera discloses pricing or if a commercial partner changes launch-price assumptions.
